sourceLine: your VR training analytics and the questions safety managers ask before they trust a VR certificate

cards.title: Measuring Transfer, Not Completion
cards.angle: A March 2026 Scientific Reports study compared VR-trained substation workers against observations at a real site, and the field is starting to ask for that kind of evidence instead of completion rates. Your LMS already captures the inputs; the follow-up design is missing.
cards.evidence: Your analytics page logs actions, decisions, accuracy and timing per trainee, while your Komatsu case reports a potential 55.13 percent time-efficiency saving per class for the 2022 cohort, a throughput figure. Logged decisions become a transfer measure only with later on-site assessment, and the article is how a safety manager designs that step.

sources.title: Virtual reality to enhance risk management and safety in electrical substations

cards.title: Where a VR Record Sits in the Evidence Trail
cards.angle: WorkSafe WA's transition for mine statutory positions ended March 30 2026, and appointees must meet role-specific criteria including examinations. A VR session is not that evidence, and your own FAQ says so.
cards.evidence: Your FAQ states the platform cannot be used solely to certify someone in a course; it supplements learning or records refresher completion, and exports data in multiple formats without naming SCORM or xAPI. The piece defines what a VR record can show (what was practiced, how the learner responded) and where it fits inside a wider assessment.

sources.title: WorkSafe extends transition period for mines statutory positions

cards.title: Headset Fleets After Quest for Business
cards.angle: Meta stopped selling commercial Quest SKUs and new managed-services subscriptions on February 20 2026, with existing Horizon Managed Services customers supported to January 4 2030. Everyone else standing up a fleet now is on consumer hardware plus third-party MDM.
cards.evidence: Your pricing page lists seven compatible headsets, your FAQ names two Pico models for bring-your-own hardware, and offline mode appears as an Unlimited-tier feature while the FAQ says downloaded courses run without WiFi. A mine-site buyer needs those three answers in one place, and reconciling them is the article.
